skill.name: designing-frontend
skill.description: Build distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces with memorable aesthetics for web components, pages, and applications.
skill.summary: Guides creative frontend implementation from concept through visual verification.
skill.author: Byunk

security_audit.summary: The four static findings are false positives caused by design vocabulary in SKILL.md. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, external command usage, or system reconnaissance behavior was found.

static_findings.snippet: - Use distinctive, characterful fonts (avoid Inter, Roboto, Arial, system fonts)
- Avoid clichéd combinations (purple gradients on white)
- Break from grid conventions: asymmetry, overlap, diagonal flow
- **Never converge**: Avoid repeated choices (Space Grotesk, common layouts)

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 33 refers to avoiding generic typography choices such as system fonts. It does not request host inspection, OS discovery, or any system reconnaissance activity.
Line 39 is a design guideline about avoiding overused color combinations. It contains no instruction to inspect a system or collect environment information.
Line 47 discusses spatial composition and layout conventions. The wording is about visual grids, not operating system discovery or reconnaissance.
Line 59 warns against repeated design choices and common layouts. It does not direct the model to probe files, commands, networks, or system state.

content.value_statement: Generic interfaces can make products feel interchangeable. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward specific visual direction, polished code, and verification.
actual_capabilities: Defines a visual concept based on purpose, user context, and constraints.
Guides implementation for HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, and Vue interfaces.
Applies typography, color, motion, layout, and background design guidance.
Encourages accessibility validation and interaction testing during verification.
Promotes varied design choices across projects to avoid generic patterns.
limitations: It provides design guidance, not a complete design system library.
It does not include bundled fonts, images, templates, or component files.
It depends on the base model and project tools for code correctness.
It requires user context to choose an appropriate aesthetic direction.

use_cases.title: Build a Product Dashboard
use_cases.description: Create a polished dashboard that matches the product domain and avoids generic SaaS styling.

use_cases.title: Refresh a Marketing Page
use_cases.description: Turn a plain page into a memorable web experience with stronger hierarchy, motion, and visual texture.

use_cases.title: Prototype a New App Screen
use_cases.description: Explore a specific aesthetic direction before converting it into production frontend code.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Landing Section
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a single page section.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the designing-frontend skill to create a landing section for a finance app. Make it distinctive, accessible, and production ready.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for polishing a component already in the project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the designing-frontend skill to redesign this component. Keep the data model, improve hierarchy, motion, color, and responsive behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Full Interface
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for a complete feature screen.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the designing-frontend skill to build a complete onboarding interface. Define the aesthetic direction, implement the screen, and verify accessibility.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Domain-Specific System
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for a broader frontend direction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the designing-frontend skill to create a visual system for a medical analytics tool. Include layout rules, components, states, and verification notes.

output_examples.input: A request for a distinctive analytics dashboard.
output_examples.output: A focused dashboard concept with domain-specific typography, structured density, restrained motion, and responsive production interface guidance.

output_examples.input: A plain signup page that feels generic.
output_examples.output: A redesigned signup flow with stronger visual hierarchy, purposeful color, polished hover states, and accessibility checks.

output_examples.input: A new product page for a creative tool.
output_examples.output: A bold page direction with expressive type, contextual visual effects, interaction details, and implementation priorities.

best_practices: Provide the product domain, audience, framework, and accessibility requirements before asking for implementation.
Ask for verification of hierarchy, responsiveness, interactions, and accessibility after the first build.
Request a specific aesthetic direction when brand or user expectations are already known.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a generic modern design without domain context.
Do not skip accessibility checks when adding animation, contrast, or dense layouts.
Do not reuse the same fonts, gradients, and layout patterns across unrelated projects.

faq.question: Does this skill write frontend code?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides the model to write production-grade HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, Vue, or similar frontend code.

faq.question: Does it include ready-made design assets?
faq.answer: No. It provides design and implementation guidance, but it does not bundle fonts, images, or templates.

faq.question: Can it help with accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow includes accessibility validation during verification, especially for interactions, contrast, and hierarchy.

faq.question: Is it only for landing pages?
faq.answer: No. It applies to components, pages, application screens, and complete frontend experiences.

faq.question: Which tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What context should users provide?
faq.answer: Provide the audience, purpose, framework, brand constraints, accessibility needs, and examples of styles to avoid.
